summary: Enable threaded incident bridge with AI summarizer and time-bound transcript archive
description:
Issue summary:
We need a new cross-pod incident bridge pattern that creates a threaded Slack channel (or private channel thread) for high-severity incidents, automatically persists a sanitized transcript to Confluence for post-incident review, and runs an opt-in AI summarizer to create a one-paragraph incident summary. The transcript must be time-bound (TTL) and auto-archived/expunged after 90 days unless retention is extended via an approval flow.

Impact:
- Improves follow-up and onboarding for postmortems by centralizing discussion threads and summaries.
- Reduces noise in primary #incidents channel by creating ephemeral threaded bridges.
- Must satisfy security/compliance requirement: transcripts must be scrubbed for PII before persistent storage and retention controlled with an approval workflow.

Request details / acceptance criteria:
1) Automation creates a locked thread or private channel per incident with standardized naming: incident-<ID>-<short-title>.
2) Bot pins incident runbook link and posts list of on-call participants.
3) At incident close the bot triggers: (a) optional AI summarizer (internal model endpoint) that produces a 3-sentence public summary, (b) scrubber that masks email addresses, API keys and other probable secrets, (c) publishes sanitized transcript to a Confluence page under OPS > Incident Archives.
4) Transcript pages get TTL metadata (90d default). A request button in Confluence allows owners to extend retention via an approval workflow routed to Security and Legal.
5) All automation actions must be auditable (Jira ticket created and linked, audit log entry for retention changes).
6) Provide toggle in admin console to enable/disable AI summarizer for specific pods.

Timeline: prefer pilot in two pods within 3 weeks, full rollout after compliance signoff.

Notes on safety: the AI summarizer must not expose raw PII; summarizer must run on private model endpoint (dedicated tier) and store only the sanitized output.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New incident thread creation verified in staging and prod; 2) Sanitizer detects and masks emails and API-like strings in a sample transcript; 3) Confluence page created with TTL metadata and a visible 'Request Retention Extension' action; 4) Jira ticket auto-created on finalization with links to thread and Confluence; 5) Admin toggle works and disables summarizer when off.
steps:
Trigger path to repro in staging:
1) Create test incident ticket INT-TEST-800 and mark severity as Sev2.
2) Use /incident-start in #incidents-staging channel and follow prompts.
3) Add a message containing an email and a fake API key.
4) Close incident and observe bot workflow: summarizer prompt, sanitizer output, Confluence page creation, TTL metadata, Jira ticket creation.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel: Filing request after retrospective — Ops and SRE requested more structured ephemeral bridges and automatic summaries to speed PM/engineering handoffs.
2026-03-12 - Marina Chen: Assigned. Planning to prototype using the existing incident-bot and a small Lambda-backed scrubber. Need security input on masking rules.

2026-03-12 - Tomás Rivera (Security): Security: list of patterns to mask (emails, bearer tokens, AWS access keys, long hex strings). Also need to ensure Confluence page ACLs default to 'ops-read, security-read'.

2026-03-13 - Marina Chen: Spiked two approaches for summarizer: (A) call internal private model via dedicated endpoint (preferred), (B) call hosted summarizer with no PII storage (needs contract). Preferring A for compliance.
2026-03-14 - Legal (D. Nguyen): Need retention policy draft and escalation path for retention extension requests. Will review Confluence workflow mockup.
investigation_notes:
- Prototype options reviewed: reuse incident-bot (python) and add post-close hook to call sanitizer service.
- Sanitizer implementation: regex-first pass + danger-signal heuristic + optional manual review for flagged tokens.
- Access control: Confluence page creation must set space to OPS Incident Archives and apply a page property 'ttl: 90d'.
- Audit concerns: add structured metadata to created Jira ticket (labels + custom field incident-thread-url).
- Dependencies: Security approval for masking rules, Confluence admin permissions to create pages via automation, and an internal model endpoint for summarizer (request to infra needed).
proposed_solution: 1) Build a small service 'bridge-controller' that subscribes to incident lifecycle events. 2) On incident-start create slack private-thread via bot user, enforce naming convention. 3) On incident-close run sanitizer, then call private summarizer endpoint if summarizer toggle is enabled for the pod. 4) Create Confluence page via API with sanitized transcript and summary, set TTL metadata and ACLs. 5) Create final Jira ticket linking to artifacts. 6) Implement an approval workflow in Confluence using page comments + a webhook that triggers a Jira approval ticket routed to Security+Legal for retention extension. 7) Add admin console toggle and a flag in pod config.
